case_name: Tarunjeet Singh Bhogal vs State Of Himachal Pradesh And Others

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Himachal Pradesh And Others

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage of Tarunjeet Singh Bhogal was solemnized with late Jaspreet Kaur. After marriage, they lived together for some time but subsequently parted ways due to a dispute.

legal_principles.principle: The power to prevent abuse of process of court can be exercised even when the discharge application is pending with the trial court.
legal_principles.held: It is settled principle of law that the High court can exercise jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C even when the discharge application is pending with the trial court
cited_cases: G. Sagar Suri and Anr. V. State of U.P. and Others, (2000) 2 SCC 636
Umesh Kumar v. State of Andhra Pradesh and Anr. (2013) 10 SCC 591
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent abuse of process and secure the ends of justice

legal_principles.principle: The inherent jurisdiction of the court can be exercised to give effect to an order under the CrPC, to prevent the abuse of the process of the court, or to otherwise secure the ends of justice.
legal_principles.held: Under Section 482 the inherent jurisdiction of the court can be exercised (i) to give effect to an order under the CrPC; (ii) to prevent the abuse of the process of the court; and (iii) to otherwise secure the ends of justice
cited_cases: Inder Mohan Goswami v State of Uttaranchal
Pramod Suryabhan Pawar v. The State of Maharashtra and Anr, (2019) 9 SCC 608
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to secure the ends of justice
